<store>
Name: Fernhill Coffee Supply
Sells: Fernhill Coffee Supply sells home coffee brewing equipment and coffee beans. The range covers pour-over gear (ceramic and stainless steel drippers, size 02 paper filters, stovetop and electric gooseneck kettles, and a brew scale with timer), immersion brewers such as a French press and a cold brew jar, and manual and electric burr grinders. It also sells single-origin coffee beans from Fernhill Roastery in 250 g and 1 kg bags, whole bean or ground.
Audience: People who brew coffee at home, especially by pour-over or immersion, and who want to grind, weigh and control water temperature themselves. Some products, such as the single-dose flat-burr grinder and the temperature-hold kettle, suit buyers who care about precise brewing.
Tone: expert
Never say: —
</store>

content.text: {"title":"How to Make Cold Brew Coffee at Home: Beans, Grind, Ratio and Steep Time","angle":"The reader will learn how cold brew works, which beans and grind size to choose, how much coffee to use, how long to steep, and how to filter, dilute and store a smooth concentrate at home.","sections":[{"heading":"What cold brew is and why it tastes different","covers":"Cold brew is an immersion method: coarse coffee steeps in cold or room-temperature water for many hours instead of minutes. Explains in general terms why it tends to taste smoother and less acidic than iced hot coffee, and the difference between cold brew and iced coffee. Introduces the Cold Brew Jar as a dedicated immersion brewer.","facts":["F2","F3"]},{"heading":"Choosing beans for cold brew","covers":"General advice: medium roasts with chocolate and caramel character are the classic, forgiving choice for cold brew, while fruity light roasts give a brighter, more unusual cup. Presents Colombia Huila as the dependable pick and Ethiopia Guji as the adventurous one. Recommends buying whole bean and grinding coarse yourself, since a filter grind is too fine for a long steep.","facts":["F11","F20","F22","F14","F41","F42","F35"]},{"heading":"Grind coarse, like for French press","covers":"Why grind size matters so much over a 12+ hour steep: too fine gives bitterness and muddy concentrate, too coarse gives weak coffee. Aim for a coarse, French-press-style grind. The Hand Grinder covers this range with click settings; be upfront that its 25 g hopper means a full jar batch takes several loads, so set the setting once and grind in rounds.","facts":["F23","F26","F27","F28"]},{"heading":"How much coffee and how long to steep","covers":"General ratio guidance for concentrate (roughly 1:5 to 1:8 coffee to water by weight) and ready-to-drink (around 1:12 to 1:15), and why weighing helps. Applies it to the jar: the filter basket holds up to 150 g of coarse coffee and the jar makes 1.5 litres of concentrate, steeped 12 to 18 hours in the fridge. Advice to start at 14 hours and adjust by taste.","facts":["F6","F7","F10","F1"]},{"heading":"Step by step with the Cold Brew Jar","covers":"Practical walkthrough: weigh and grind the coffee, fill the stainless steel filter basket, pour in cold filtered water slowly to wet all grounds, close the airtight lid, refrigerate in the fridge door, then lift out the basket after steeping. Notes the glass jar lets you see the brew, and the fine filter keeps sediment out of the concentrate.","facts":["F4","F5","F8","F9","F10"]},{"heading":"Diluting, serving and storing your concentrate","covers":"General advice on diluting concentrate 1:1 with water or milk over ice, adjusting to strength, ideas like adding tonic, and keeping the concentrate sealed and cold, typically drinking it within about a week to ten days for best flavour.","facts":["F7","F8"]},{"heading":"No dedicated jar? Use a French press","covers":"How to make a smaller batch of cold brew in a French press: coarse grounds and cold water in the beaker, steep covered in the fridge, then press and decant so it doesn't keep extracting. Suits people who already own one or want a multi-use brewer.","facts":["F52","F53","F58","F59"]}],"products":["P1","P2","P3","P6"],"links":["P1","P2","P4","P3","P6","L3","L2","L4"]}
